title: Automated Microservice Build Orchestration
business: A cloud-native fintech startup managing dozens of independent microservices.
problem: Manual build scripts and inconsistent CI environments lead to deployment drift and frequent integration failures during the release cycle.
solution: Implementing Tekton Pipelines allows the team to define reusable, version-controlled build steps as Kubernetes custom resources, ensuring that every microservice follows a standardized, immutable build process within the cluster.
steps: Define individual build steps as Task resources to encapsulate specific logic like unit testing or container image building.
Compose these Tasks into a Pipeline resource to define the sequential execution order for the microservice build.
Configure a PipelineRun to trigger the execution of the defined Pipeline against a specific source code repository.
Utilize the Tekton Catalog to pull pre-verified, reusable Task definitions for common operations like Git cloning or image pushing.
outcome: Standardized build artifacts and reduced configuration drift across the microservice architecture, leading to more reliable and predictable deployment cycles.
limitation: Tekton resources are stored as Kubernetes objects, which can lead to cluster state bloat if old PipelineRuns are not pruned; check this by monitoring the count of completed PipelineRun resources in the namespace.
